text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Clinton hopeful on Syrian peace talk track.
- Bank workers strike today.
- Outrage over marketing in U.S. of cookbook of recipes written by prisoners in World War Two concentration camp.
- Croatian president appeals for ties with Israel.

- Bank Discount share issue delayed following Securities Authority's failure to approve offering of 17 percent. Authority was to approve prospectus on Thursday but instead decided to ask Discount for more information on fourth quarter 1996. Offer expected to be delayed for about one month.
HAARETZ
- Clinton tells Israel's Netanyahu he will work to renew Israel's negotiations with Syria.
- Commission investigating helicopter disaster in which 73 Israeli soldiers were killed to give interim findings to defence minister today; final report expected in month.
- Bank branches to be closed due to strike. Workers demanding five-day work week.
- Signs that in February budget deficit estimate will also be overshot.
- Discount offering delayed while Securities Authority seeks more information.
- Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel not proposing another budget cut, rather closer attention to framework.
- Transport minister says he still insists El Al airline will not fly on Jewish sabbath even after privatisation.
MAARIV
- Clinton says Israel is the one to decide how to act on its northern border.
- Commission on helicopter disaster: Flight was not according to regulations.
- Coordinator of fight against "terrorism" says there is danger "terror" groups could use nonconventional weapons.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Estimate in air force: at the end of helicopter investigation senior figures will have to make conclusions.
- Netanyahu to Clinton: There is no chance of a full withdrawal from the Golan Heights.
- Five percent rise in couples divorcing in 1996.

- Poll: 59 pct of Israelis think Jews involved in killings of Arabs for nationalist motives should be freed after release of several Palestinian female prisoners who killed Jews; 31 pct think no need to release the Jews; 10 pct no answer.
- Hamas official Marzook held in United States pending extradition interviewed on wide range of subjects.
GLOBES
- Finance Minister Meridor says government will have to have another process of budget cutting; raising taxes is a negative step.
- Discount trying to prevent cancellation of share offering.
